title: The evening examen
tomorrow: what were Jesus's last words in Luke, and where did he get them?

cards: Lights off, phone on the charger, and the day starts replaying on its own: the thing you said, the message you sent too fast, the face someone made. The replay usually asks one question, what went wrong.
Saint Ignatius of Loyola taught a short evening practice that asks a better one first. It's called the examen, and it doesn't start with blame. It starts with thanks.

teach.b: In the Spiritual Exercises, Ignatius lays it out in a few plain steps. Give thanks to God for the gifts of the day. Ask for light to see it truly.
Go back through the day hour by hour, from the moment you woke. Ask pardon where it's needed.
Then resolve, with God's help, to do better tomorrow. Notice the order. Thanks comes before faults, and light comes before the looking.
It echoes a much older evening review.

teach.h: GOD SAW, AND IT WAS VERY GOOD.
teach.b: At the end of the sixth day in Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims: "God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good." So try it on this week. A road walked with eyes up.
A first task offered. A minute at noon. A slump you stayed through.
A blessing at the door. A table faced together.
Where was God in any of it? Some of those went well and some didn't. The examen holds both, and it starts with the good.

how: Jesuits and many other Catholics pray the examen each evening, and some also at midday; a short examination of conscience is part of Night Prayer.

o: a nightly look back over the day with God

games.q: your friend says today was a total loss: a fight, a bad grade, a missed bus. by the examen, where does she start?
o: with one thing to be thankful for.
with the fight, since it matters most.
with a plan to fix tomorrow.
games.why: Ignatius puts thanks first, then light, then the day hour by hour. the fight gets its turn, but not first.

practice: Go back through today from the moment you woke, slowly, like scrolling a camera roll. Stop at one moment you're grateful for and one you'd take back. Ask quietly, of each, where God was in it.

wordCard.voice: The evening examen. Ignatius's short look back over the day: thanks first, then light, then pardon, then tomorrow.

carryVoice: Your line: where was God, asked once before sleep. A good week, and it's done.
